subject: art-design
title: Sketchbook Development: Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch your sketchbook into a portfolio-quality resource — coherent, cross-referenced and reflective.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE sketchbook work: cross-referencing, contextual research, reflective journals.
final_note: A great sketchbook is half artwork, half thinking.

concepts.def: Linking pages and ideas across the book.
Honest review of what worked or did not.
How clearly the book tells one story.
Curated body of work shown together.
Combining sources into your own idea.

walkthroughs.body_html: Strong contextual research goes beyond Wikipedia. Visit galleries, read interviews, watch documentaries. Quote artists in their own words and react with sketches. This depth pushes work into higher mark bands.

Cross-reference by numbering pages and using arrows: "see p.14 for first idea, developed here from p.22". This shows examiners how decisions evolved — and makes the sketchbook feel like a single argument, not a stack of pages.

Add a short reflection at the bottom of each spread — two sentences max. "This experiment failed because the paper buckled, so I will try heavier stock". Reflective practice turns mistakes into next moves and proves synthesis.
